description: Direct attempts at forbidden actions, invoked straight against the action layer with no agent in the call stack.

cases.title: An approver approves their own request
cases.commentary: The first of the three rules a reader should not need explained. Invoked directly, so nothing in the agent path is load-bearing.

cases.title: An approver approves above their authorization threshold
cases.commentary: $12,000 against a $10,000 threshold. The margin is small on purpose: the rule is an inequality, not a heuristic.

cases.title: A deactivated principal decides a request
cases.commentary: Sam's threshold would permit this. Sam is deactivated, and the rule that catches it is about the principal rather than the amount.

cases.title: A request is approved before it is submitted
cases.commentary: A DRAFT has had no review. Approving one skips the step rather than violating it, which is why the state machine is a gate and not a display.
